 How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support 
 How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone
 Most iPhone models can charge with MagSafe Charger.
 Set up your MagSafe Charger
 Connect the USB-C connector on your MagSafe Charger to a recommended 30W or greater Apple USB-C power adapter or compatible third-party USB-C adapter. You can also connect to a USB-C port on a Mac or PC.
 Place your MagSafe Charger face up—as shown—on a flat surface, clear of any metal objects or other foreign material.
 Place your iPhone on your MagSafe Charger.
 Get up to 25W faster wireless charging
 The MagSafe Charger is designed to quickly and safely wirelessly charge your iPhone. The system intelligently adapts to conditions to optimize charging your iPhone at up to 25W of peak power delivery for faster wireless charging. The actual power delivered to the iPhone will vary depending on the iPhone model, wattage of the power adapter, and system conditions.
 It's important to plug into a power source before placing your iPhone on the MagSafe Charger. This allows MagSafe to verify it's safe to deliver maximum power. If you happen to place your iPhone on the MagSafe Charger before plugging into a power source, simply remove your iPhone from the MagSafe Charger, wait three seconds, and then put it back on to resume maximum power delivery.
 All power adapters have different ratings for amount and rate of power delivery. The MagSafe Charger requires the following ratings to deliver faster wireless charging.
 Use these power adapters and iPhone models together for up to 25W faster wireless charging
 iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPhone 17, iPhone 16 Plus, and iPhone 16 Pro Max
 30W or greater power adapter
 15V/2.0A or higher power adapter
 MagSafe Charger, noted on the device or its cable as part number A3502, A3503, A2580, or A3250
 Higher wattage adapters at or above 15V/2.0A will also deliver a maximum of up to 25W peak power to your iPhone.
 iPhone Air will achieve 20W peak power. iPhone 16 and iPhone 16 Pro will achieve 22.5W peak power.
 While you have USB-C or Lightning accessories such as headphones connected to your phone, charging is limited to 16W for iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max; 10W for iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max; 7.5W for iPhone 16, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16 Pro, and iPhone 16 Pro Max; and limited to 16W for iPhone 17 and iPhone Air to comply with regulatory standards.
 Use these power adapters and iPhone models together for up to 15W faster wireless charging
 iPhone 17e, iPhone 15 and earlier
 20W or greater USB-C power adapter
 9V/2.22A or 9V/2.56A or higher power adapter*
 MagSafe Charger, noted on the device or its cable as part number A2140
 For iPhone 15 and earlier, when USB-C or Lightning accessories such as headphones are connected, charging is limited to 7.5W to comply with regulatory standards. iPhone 13 mini and iPhone 12 mini can get up to 12W for faster wireless charging with at least 9V/2.03A
 *The MagSafe Charger will also function with power adapters that provide a minimum 12W (5V/2.4A) of power, but this will result in slower charging.
 Learn more
 Your MagSafe Charger is designed for faster and most efficient charging with Apple MagSafe accessories and these iPhone models:
 iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone 18 Pro
 iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPhone 17e, iPhone Air
 iPhone 16 Pro Max, iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16
 iPhone 15 models
 iPhone 14 models
 iPhone 13 models
 iPhone 12 models
 Power and charge times are different when you use a MagSafe Charger to charge a non-MagSafe, Qi-compatible device such as iPhone 16e, iPhone 11 models, iPhone X, iPhone XS models, iPhone XR, and iPhone 8 models.
 With iPhone 15 and later models, if you're in the European Union or in a country or region that's part of the European Free Trade Association, the first time that you use a wireless charger, you'll get a notification. Mandated by the EU, the notification says that wireless charging might use more power than wired charging.
 Don't place credit cards, security badges, passports, or key fobs between your iPhone and MagSafe Charger, because this might damage magnetic strips or RFID chips in those items. If you have a case that holds any of these sensitive items, remove them before charging or make sure that they aren’t between the back of your device and the charger. Learn about the magnets in MagSafe products .
 If your iPhone is connected to both a MagSafe Charger and power through its Lightning or USB-C connector, your iPhone will charge via the connector.
 As with other wireless chargers, your iPhone or MagSafe Charger might get slightly warmer while your iPhone charges. To extend the lifespan of your battery, if the battery gets too warm, software might limit charging above 80 percent. 
 Apple’s MagSafe wireless charging provides optimal magnetic alignment for faster, more efficient charging. MagSafe wireless charging includes technologies that reduce energy waste when compared to other wireless charging methods.

 Fast charge your iPhone - Apple Support 
 Fast charge your iPhone
 Find out what you need to fast charge your iPhone.
 What you need
 iPhone 18 Pro models and iPhone Duo
 To fast charge iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max up to 50 percent battery in around 15 minutes, or iPhone Duo up to 50 percent battery in around 20 minutes, use the USB-C cable that came in the box, and one of these adapters:
 Apple 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max
 A comparable third-party 60W-capable (or greater) adapter that uses Adjustable Voltage Supply (AVS) and supports USB Power Delivery (USB-PD) 3.2
 iPhone 17 models and iPhone Air
 You can fast charge iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, and iPhone 17 Pro Max up to 50 percent battery in around 20 minutes with a 40W adapter or higher. For iPhone 17e and iPhone Air, use a 20W adapter or higher to charge up to 50 percent battery in around 30 minutes.
 Earlier iPhone models
 To fast charge an iPhone 15 or later, use a USB-C cable , like the one that came in the box, or use a USB-C to Lightning cable with an earlier iPhone model. You need one of these adapters:
 Apple 18W or greater USB-C Power Adapter
 A comparable third-party USB-C power adapter that supports USB-PD
 Wireless fast charging
 To wirelessly charge iPhone 18 Pro models and iPhone Duo up to 50 percent in around 30 minutes, use a MagSafe Charger and a 35W or higher adapter.
 For iPhone 16, iPhone 17, and iPhone Air use a MagSafe Charger and one of these adapters:
 Apple 30W or greater USB-C Power Adapter
 A comparable third-party USB-C power adapter that supports USB Power Delivery (USB-PD)

 A comparable third-party USB-C power adapter that supports USB Power Delivery (USB-PD)
 Fast charging might not work in conditions that are too cold or too hot .

 iPhone 17 Models Likely to Support 25W Wireless Third-Party Chargers
 Tuesday July 15, 2025 8:31 am PDT by Tim Hardwick 
 Apple's forthcoming iPhone 17 models are likely to support up to 25W wireless charging using a variety of third-party MagSafe charging accessories, thanks to compatibility with the next-generation Qi 2.2 wireless charging standard.
Currently, iPhones featuring MagSafe use Qi 2, the Wireless Power Consortium's (WPC) widely supported second-generation charging standard. With third-party chargers, Qi 2 maxes out at 15W – although iPhone 16 models do support upgraded 25W MagSafe charging using an official 30W Apple charger .
 That limitation is likely to change with the iPhone 17 models, which are expected to support Qi 2.2, based on regulatory filings for updated MagSafe Chargers on Taiwan's NCC certification website. It was originally believed – and widely reported – that the WPC's Qi 2.2 standard would support up to 50W output. However, this turned out to be based on incorrect information. Qi 2.2 officially supports up to 25W . 
Expect iPhone-compatible third-party Qi 2.2 chargers to become increasingly prevalent as we edge closer to the launch of the iPhone 17 lineup in September. For example, Ugreen has already announced its MagFlow Magnetic Power Bank, which it says is the first in the world to receive official Qi 2.2 certification from the WPC. The power bank is set to launch across the US, Europe, and Southeast Asian markets in the third quarter of this year.
 In addition to faster charging, Qi 2.2 offers improved magnetic alignment and charging efficiency compared to its predecessor. The standard also features backward compatibility with older Qi chargers.

 How to Charge iPhone 17: Fast Wired & Wireless Options
 03/06/2026 | Anker 
 Blog Center Chargers Power Banks Wireless Chargers Hubs & Docks Others 
 All 
 Just upgraded? You might be wondering how to charge iPhone 17 with all the options Apple built in. The phone supports faster wired speeds, improved MagSafe, and the newer Qi2 25W standard, which means you have more ways than ever to power it up, at home, at work, or on the go. This guide walks you through each method and helps you choose the one that fits your routine.
 Table of contents

 How to Charge iPhone 17: Best Chargers 
 What Should I Pay Attention to When Charging the iPhone 17? 
 Conclusion 
 FAQs 
 Different iPhone 17 Charging Ways
 The iPhone 17 gives you several ways to charge, from fast wired USB-C options to newer magnetic wireless standards. Below, you'll find a simple, practical look at each method:
 USB-C port wired charging
 The USB-C port on the bottom of the phone is still the quickest and most reliable way to charge. Apple includes a USB-C to USB-C cable in the box, but you'll need your own power adapter .
 Will iPhone 17 have fast charging? Well, yes, with the right charger , you get the fastest results:
 The iPhone 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max can all about 50% in roughly 20 minutes when paired with a 40W or higher USB-C PD adapter .
 That's noticeably faster than older iPhones, which needed a 20W or higher adapter and took around 30 minutes to hit the same 50% mark.
 Any good-quality USB-C Power Delivery (PD) charger at 40W or above will work. It doesn't need to be Apple-branded.
 Use wired USB-C charging when:
 You're low on battery and need a quick boost.
 You want less heat and better long-term battery health.
 You're traveling and can plug into walls, trains, or airplane outlets.
 MagSafe wireless charging
 MagSafe is Apple's magnetic wireless charging system. The ring of magnets on the back of the iPhone 17 snaps onto a MagSafe puck or stand so the coils line up correctly without guesswork. It makes wireless charging much easier and helps the phone stay at its best charging speed.
 On the iPhone 17, MagSafe works the same way it does on the iPhone 16 series, but it's noticeably faster than older iPhone 12-15 models:
 The iPhone 17 supports up to 25W MagSafe charging when paired with a 30W or higher power adapter.
 With that setup, you can reach around 50% in about 30 minutes , which is close to the old wired fast-charging speeds.
 Older iPhones (12-15) cap MagSafe at 15W and typically take about 45 minutes to hit 50%.
 MagSafe works best when you want a clean, drop-and-go routine, on a nightstand, a desk, or even in the car. It also plays nicely with magnetic stands, tripods, and wallets. Just remember that wireless charging is still slower than a cable, and thick or metal cases can reduce performance.
 Qi2 25W wireless charging
 Qi2 is the newer open wireless-charging standard inspired by MagSafe's magnetic alignment. It uses the same idea: magnets that snap your phone into place, so the charger delivers power more efficiently.
 Here's how Qi2 wireless charging breaks down on the iPhone 17:
 The first wave of Qi2 chargers matched 15W , similar to first-gen MagSafe speeds.
 The newer Qi2 standard now reaches the same 25W speeds as Apple's latest MagSafe.
 The iPhone 17 supports Qi2 25W out of the box , giving you about 50% in around 30 minutes when paired with a capable adapter.
 The biggest advantage of Qi2 is choice. You aren't limited to Apple's puck; you'll find Qi2-certified chargers from many trusted third-party brands, like Anker. They come in all kinds of designs: slim flat pads, upright stands, multi-device docks, and magnetic car chargers .
 Power bank charging
 If you charge on the move, a power bank is your best friend. Modern power banks support both wired USB-C charging and wireless magnetic charging , giving you flexibility wherever you are.
 Here's what each type offers for your iPhone 17:
 USB-C power banks: Plug in with a USB-C cable for the fastest speeds. Most banks offer 20-30W USB-C PD output , which is already enough to hit the phone's higher charging rates. Some models push 40W, 60W, or even 140W , meaning they can easily fast-charge your iPhone 17 or have enough power to run a laptop or tablet.
 MagSafe or Qi2 magnetic power banks: These snap to the back of your phone and give you true cable-free power on the go. Most support 7.5-15W wireless charging , and when you connect a USB-C cable instead, they can usually deliver 18-30W .
 Power banks are great for long days out, commutes, travel, or any situation where you'd rather not search for a wall outlet.
 Reverse charging
 Reverse charging lets your phone act like a mini power bank for other devices. On the iPhone 17, this feature works only through a USB-C cable , not wirelessly.
 Wired reverse charging (supported) 
 You can plug small devices directly into your iPhone 17 using a USB-C cable . The phone then shares its battery with:
 AirPods
 Another iPhone
 Small accessories
 The iPhone 17 outputs up to about 4.5W , which is enough to give earbuds or another phone a quick bump of power. It's best for emergency top-ups, not full charges.
 Reverse wireless charging (not supported on iPhone) 
 Some Android phones can wirelessly charge earbuds or another phone by placing the device on the back. Despite the rumors, Apple hasn't added this feature to the iPhone 17. Reports after launch suggest Apple skipped it again because it's harder to make wireless reverse charging work reliably with the strong MagSafe magnets.
 So, when you hear about "reverse charging" for iPhone 17, it refers to the USB-C wired version only.
 That said, if someone near you has a compatible Android phone, like a Samsung Galaxy S25, they can wirelessly reverse-charge your iPhone 17. The feature just isn't available in the other direction.
 How to Charge iPhone 17: Best Chargers
 Need a new 17 iPhone charger? Below are some of the best charger options from Anker you can trust, from fast USB-C and MagSafe to Qi2 25W and power banks. Each one fills a different need, so you can pick what fits your routine the most.
 USB-C Charger
 Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, GaNPrime) 
 If you want one compact brick that can handle your iPhone, your laptop, and anything else you carry, this Anker Prime Charger (160W) is built for that kind of setup.
 It offers three USB-C ports with 160W total output , and a single port can reach up to 140W , which is more than enough for a high-power 16" MacBook Pro. It's powered by Anker's GaNPrime 2.0 system with PowerIQ 5.0 , so it adjusts power across devices intelligently and keeps heat under control with ActiveShield 4.0 .
 The AnkerSense View screen is surprisingly useful. It shows the exact wattage each port is drawing in real time , which makes it easy to see when your iPhone or laptop is getting a fast charge. You can tap the button below the display to swap between AI-managed modes or your own custom settings, or connect through the Anker app to check everything over Bluetooth.
 Even with all that power inside, the charger stays impressively compact, roughly the size of an AirPods Pro 3 case, so it works well as a single charger for travel or for keeping your desk uncluttered.
 Anker Prime USB-C to USB-C Cable (3 ft, 240W, Upcycled-Braided) 
 Need a spare USB-C cable? This Anker Prime USB-C to USB-C Cable is built for long-term use and consistent fast charging. It's rated for up to 240W , so it easily supports the iPhone 17's fast-charge needs while also working for high-power laptops.
 The upcycled braided jacket is tested for more than 300,000 bends and can handle up to 220 lbs of pull. It's USB-IF certified , carries 480 Mbps data, and is designed to keep working in extreme temperatures from -40°F to 176°F .
 In everyday use, it simply behaves like a cable you don't need to think about: durable, reliable, and safe for every device you charge.
 MagSafe Charger
 Anker 3-in-1 Cube with MagSafe 
 This Anker 3-in-1 Cube with Qi2 is a neat way to charge your iPhone , Apple Watch , and AirPods at the same time, all without cables.
 It's an official Made for MagSafe charger, so your iPhone 17 snaps into place with proper alignment and charges at 15W MagSafe speeds . The other sides of the cube pop out to reveal charging spots for your watch and earbuds.
 It pops up your iPhone 17 into an adjustable stand with up to 60° tilt , so it's easy to glance at notifications, use StandBy mode, or watch a quick video while the phone charges.
 The whole unit folds into a compact cube that fits in a small bag or even a large pocket. One outlet and one cable take care of your core Apple setup, which is perfect for hotel stays or a small bedside table.
 Qi2 25W wireless charger
 Anker Prime Wireless Charging Station (Qi2 25W, 3-in-1 Stand) 
 This Anker Prime Wireless Charging Station is built for people who want fast, reliable wireless charging and a tidy setup for their iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods. It uses the latest Qi2 25W-certified magnetic charging , which can take an iPhone 17 Pro to around 50% in about 22 minutes , so you get speeds that feel close to wired charging.
 The stand's sleek V-rod design supports your phone at a comfortable angle for StandBy mode or quick glances at notifications. And it's Apple-certified for fast charging your Apple Watch .
 On top of that, it includes several features that make everyday charging easier:
 Aerospace-grade TEC active cooling: A small thermal-electric module sits behind the charging surface to keep your phone below 89°F while charging. Lower heat helps preserve long-term battery health and keeps charging speeds consistent.
 ActiveShield 5.0 safety: The station monitors temperature more than 10 million times a day , adjusting power when needed to maintain safe, steady charging.
 1.65" live display: A small screen shows real-time power, temperature, and charging status. You can switch it to a simple screensaver, and it can show quick alerts if something needs attention.
 Three smart charging modes: 
 Boost Mode: for quick top-ups with light cooling.
 Ice Mode: for maximum cooling and the fastest possible charge when you're actively using your phone。
 Sleep Mode: dims the display and quiets the fan for overnight charging
 You can connect through NFC or Bluetooth in the Anker app to check charging status, switch modes, schedule Sleep Mode at night, or adjust settings without touching the stand.
 Anker Prime Wireless Car Charger (Qi2 25W) 
 For the car, this Anker Prime Wireless Car Charger brings Qi2 25W snap-on charging to your vent or dashboard. You can navigate, stream audio, and charge at the same time without dealing with cables each time you get in the car.
 It uses strong MagGo-style alignment, so your iPhone 17 stays locked in place even on bumpy roads . It also has AirCool active cooling , which helps maintain steady charging performance on hot days or during navigation.
 With 25W wireless speed, your phone can gain a meaningful amount of charge even on short drives, much faster than older 7.5W or 15W car chargers.
 Power bank
 Anker Prime Power Bank (26K, 300W) 
 If you travel with a laptop and your iPhone 17, this Anker Prime Power Bank (26K) can act like a mobile wall outlet.
 The 26,250mAh capacity (99.75Wh) keeps it within airline limits while giving you plenty of extra power. It offers 300W total output across two USB-C ports and one USB-A port, with up to 140W available from a single USB-C port.
 It also supports up to 250W of input , meaning you can recharge it extremely quickly, around 50% in roughly 13 minutes with a strong enough charger. A built-in screen and app support give you insight into how your devices draw power. If you work on the go or travel often, this bank can keep your iPhone 17, tablet, and laptop going for hours.
 Anker Nano Power Bank (5K, MagGo, Slim) 
 This ultra-slim Anker Nano Power Bank (5K) is designed for quick top-ups without adding bulk. It supports 15W Qi2-certified magnetic wireless charging and 20W USB-C input/output, so you can choose between cable-free convenience and faster wired charging. 
 It has a very slim body, around 103 × 70.6 × 8.6 mm , similar to a stack of cards. You can snap it to the back of your iPhone 17 and slip both into a pocket without a big bulge.
 Thermal controls help keep the charging surface cooler and protect your phone's battery by pausing charging at 80% when things get too warm. It's a good "just in case" bank for evenings out, events, and short trips , giving you enough power to get home without carrying something heavy.
 What Should I Pay Attention to When Charging the iPhone 17?
 Charging the iPhone 17 is simple, but a few habits can help your battery stay healthy and your charging stay fast.
 Keep an eye on heat
 iPhones charge best when they stay cool. Heat is the main thing that wears down lithium-ion batteries over time.
 Try to charge in a cool spot with some airflow.
 Avoid charging under pillows, blankets, or in direct sunlight.
 If the phone feels hot, remove the case or move it somewhere cooler.
 Heavy apps, like games or long video recordings, also add extra heat, so try not to run them while fast charging.
 Let iOS handle battery protection
 The iPhone 17 has several built-in tools that protect battery health in the background.
 Optimized Battery Charging pauses around 80% and completes closer to when you usually unplug.
 Charge Limiting features help keep the battery from sitting at 100% for hours.
 Adaptive Power adjusts performance and background activity to stretch battery life.
 Leave these features on unless you have a specific need to disable them. They're designed to manage everyday charging without you having to think about it.
 Try not to run the battery to 0%
 Lithium-ion batteries don't need full drain cycles, and hitting 0% too often can add stress. Plug in when you drop into low percentages instead of waiting until the phone shuts off. It's fine if it reaches 0% once in a while; just avoid making it a habit.
 Use safe, high-quality chargers and cables
 Poor-quality accessories can cause unstable power, slower charging, or overheating. Use chargers and cables from trusted brands and look for USB-C Power Delivery (PD) support. For wireless charging, choose MagSafe or Qi2-certified products that list iPhone compatibility. Replace any damaged cables as soon as you spot fraying or bent connectors.
 Overnight charging is okay with protections on
 It's safe to charge overnight as long as the phone can stay cool. With features like Optimized Battery Charging, the phone slows down near the top of the charge and finishes closer to your usual wake-up time.
 Conclusion
 Knowing how to charge iPhone 17 gives you more control over speed, convenience, and long-term battery health. Whether you prefer fast USB-C, MagSafe/Qi2 magnetic wireless charging, or a power bank on busy days, the iPhone 17 handles each method well as long as you use quality accessories and keep heat in check. And if you want reliable chargers that match the phone's full charging potential, Anker offers several options that pair perfectly with Apple's latest lineup.
 FAQs
 Does iPhone 17 come with a charger?
 No, it doesn't. Like recent iPhone models, the iPhone 17 doesn't include a power adapter in the box. You'll find a USB-C to USB-C cable, but you'll need to use your own charger or buy one separately. Any quality USB-C charger that supports USB Power Delivery (PD) will work safely with the phone, though you'll get the fastest speeds with a 40W or higher adapter.
 Can I charge my new iPhone 17 with an old charger?
 Yes, in most cases, you can. If your old charger has a USB-C port and supports USB Power Delivery (PD), it will charge the iPhone 17 without issue. Older 20W-35W chargers still work well, though a 40W or higher adapter will deliver the fastest speeds (about 50% in roughly 20 minutes).
 If your charger uses USB-A, you'll need a USB-A to USB-C cable, but charging will be slower. Lightning cables from older iPhones won't fit the new port.
 Can I use an old USB cable on the new iPhone?
 It depends on the type. The iPhone 17 uses USB-C, so Lightning cables from older iPhones no longer fit. If you already own USB-C to USB-C cables, for example, from a recent iPad or MacBook, you can reuse them. Just make sure they're in good condition and support USB-PD to ensure safe, efficient charging.
 What is the best way to charge the iPhone 17?
 To charge your iPhone 17 series, the best way is to use a 40W or higher USB-C Power Delivery charger with a high-quality USB-C cable for the fastest and safest charging. Choose Apple or certified Anker USB-C PD chargers for iPhone 17 to prolong lifespan, while MagSafe or Qi2 wireless chargers at 25W (also known as Qi2.2) are also ideal for convenient daily top-ups.
